bifurcation.note: Declared before any frame was opened. Every judgement here is a DECISIONS question — whether the screen refuses what seam S35 forbids and records only what the body did. No art-direction or fidelity call is made; the four screenshots are evidence of STATE (how much ground is revealed, how many squares) and are never judged for their look.

reference_items.native_scale: 0-10 band; 10 = every marker convention structurally impossible on every surface, adversarially, and S35-as-amended-by-S38's four hard fails all held
reference_items.native_verdict: Morrowind ships a map and ships no quest markers; RI-UIX02 is the enforcement item, ARBITRATION S35 is the specification, and S38 amends S35 in place to bind the DERIVATION rather than the authenticity of a save file
reference_items.justification: Judged against ARBITRATION S35 AS AMENDED BY S38, which landed in the working tree during this run. The permitted list is fully built and the forbidden list is structurally refused: no markers, no routes, no numerals, no travel, no 'show on map' from the journal, a square only after standing, a name only from pois.json, and undiscovered genuinely unrendered (the draw loop skips it; a fresh map paints 0 of 42,846 cells). S38's clauses (a) and (b) hold well — RESTORE_READS is ['stood'] and the arbiter's gate is 6/6 exhaustive over all 42,846 generators, which I re-ran rather than inherited, with its --control=pre-s38 going red 4 of 6. What fails is (c) and (d): sim.discovery is a writable slot the quest machine holds and window.__ENGINE reaches, so the drawn map can stop being a function of the footprint without any claim to have stood anywhere; and the seven-field load audit is computed and never published, so on the forgery that writes no claims the two fields S38-4 reads are both zero while missing_cells is 42,846 and nothing can see it.
reference_items.why_not_ten: Two clauses of S38 fail. (c): sim.discovery is writable and configurable, questEngine.sim === sim, and window.__ENGINE reaches the same slot outside every capability prohibition — 3 and 2 squares rendered respectively, from a model the game never built. (d): the itemisation exists on Discovery.lastRestore and dies there; no published surface carries it, and S38-4 cannot see the gap because it only ever forges the claim fields.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Freeze the slot (one line) and publish the audit restore() already computes. Then extend S38-4 with an arm that forges `stood` with cells:"" and places:[] and requires a moved audit field to be readable from the published surface.

reference_items.native_verdict: mandatory under ARBITRATION §3 for every model shipped
reference_items.justification: The ablation is real and the arms are comparable, and the check has been shown able to notice a consumer when one exists (--break consumer turns G2 green). But no entity reads the model: the world hash is byte-identical with the model fully destroyed. SCORING §1.1 note, as the validator asks in prose: G2 is MEASURED and FAILING, not unmeasurable, so the fail-closed-at-0 rule for an unmeasurable axis does not apply. The axis is scored 4 rather than 0 because the item's own ladder credits a real, instrumented, falsifiable model with a demonstrated data->model->pixel chain; what it has none of is an entity. Round 1 scored the same axis 4 on the same reasoning and I see no cause to move it.
reference_items.why_not_ten: Zero world-side consumers. Every reader of sim.discovery is ui/system.js, harness/api.js, save/state.js or engine.js; nothing under game/src/sim/ reads it. The pixel-level data->model->pixel chain the builder's probe demonstrates is real and well built, but a pixel is not an entity.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Give one entity a reason to read where the player has been — a guide who will not lead you somewhere you have already been, a rumour that changes once you have stood in the place it names, or a price that moves with how much of the province a trader knows you have crossed.

ar1.not_applicable_reason: The map is a menu screen and pauses the world outside combat. No fight occurs in this piece, no world value read by the map depends on player level, and the discovery model is a pure function of the cells the body occupied.

checks.observed: Nothing in the map's model reads player level, quest state or reputation. Engine._uiCtx().map is a closed list of {discovery, field, regions, pois, doc, regionName}; sim.quest is deliberately absent from it.

On the drawn map: markers 0, routes_drawn 0, numeric_text none, travel_affordances none, quest_bearing_elements none, reachable_from_journal false. No arrow, pin, waypoint, route, distance or bearing on any of the four frames.

No API by which a quest could NAME a place on the map: 13 attempts on the model's own surface all refused; observe() is arity 0; RESTORE_READS is ['stood']; the instance is frozen and the fields are #private. No quest module under game/src/sim/quest/ reaches a map module.

A quest could not name a place, but anything holding `sim` can REPLACE the model: sim.discovery is writable and configurable, questEngine.sim === sim (3 squares rendered), and window.__ENGINE reaches the same slot outside any capability prohibition (2 squares). Recorded as a concern rather than an AR-2 trigger because no quest FILE or HOOK can express it and api.js:272 discloses the route honestly.

ar3.justification: The map creates no interaction crossing the Souls/Morrowind seam. A record of where you have been is legitimately internal, and S35 requires wayfinding to keep working with the map closed — world/province.js signposts already carry it. Recorded for RI-CMP01's floor, same as round 1.

S38 clause (c): sim.discovery is a writable, configurable slot that the quest machine holds AND that window.__ENGINE reaches outside every capability prohibition — 3 and 2 squares drawn from a model the game never built, with no claim to have stood anywhere. S38's own gate audits the model's members, not the slot the model sits in.

S38 clause (d): the seven-field load audit restore() computes is never published. On the forgery that writes no claims, `dropped` and `phantom_cells` — the two fields S38-4 reads — are both ZERO while `missing_cells` is 42,846, and no published surface carries any of it.

biggest_gap.what: Discovery.restore() computes a seven-field audit of the loaded footprint against the blob's own claims — dropped, phantom_cells, missing_cells, claimed_places, derived_places, stood_cells, legacy — and every published surface throws it away: save/state.js:676 keeps only .dropped and mapState() publishes only dropped_on_load. ARBITRATION S38 clause (d) makes 'a discrepancy between the blob's claims and the derivation is ITEMISED, not swallowed' a hard fail, and the S38 gate's own assertion for it (S38-4) cannot see this gap, because S38-4 forges the CLAIM FIELDS — an all-ones raster and all 42 names — and so always produces an itemisation to read. The forgery a forger would actually write supplies no claims at all: with cells:"" and places:[] the two fields S38-4 reads are both ZERO on a save that fills the entire province, while missing_cells reads 42,846 and derived_places reads 42.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: S38 deliberately gave up tamper-resistance and kept, in exchange, the promise that a save whose claims disagree with its own derivation is itemised rather than swallowed. That promise is currently unkeepable by any instrument: the signal exists for one function call and then goes out of scope. It is also round 1's remedy 1, unactioned, and it is the difference between a build that can report on its own loads and one that cannot. The second-order cost is worse: the new gate reads green on the clause, so the gap is now covered by a passing check.

remedy.action: (1) PUBLISH THE AUDIT: carry the whole lastRestore record onto sim in save/state.js (which currently keeps only .dropped at :676) and surface it through Engine.mapState() and UISystem.state()'s `map` block, alongside the existing dropped_on_load. (2) EXTEND S38-4 TO THE SILENT FORGERY: add an arm to tools/map/arbiter-map-s38.mjs that forges `stood` with cells:"" and places:[] and requires at least one moved audit field to be readable from the published surface — as it stands, clause (d)'s gate passes on the one save shape a forger would write. (3) REPLACE map-probe L3, which forges world.discovery.places and is green; S38 already names S38-3 as its replacement. (4) FREEZE THE SLOT: Object.defineProperty(sim, 'discovery', {value: d, writable: false, configurable: false}) after construction — one line, and it closes clause (c) as well.
remedy.acceptance: node tools/harness/critic-map-r2.mjs reports A5 and A13 green: on a forged footprint with cells:"" and places:[], at least one of missing_cells / stood_cells / derived_places is readable through mapState() or getUIState().map. AND node tools/map/arbiter-map-s38.mjs still reports 6/6 with the new silent-forgery arm included, and --control=pre-s38 still exits 1. AND node tools/harness/critic-map-r2.mjs reports Q1/Q2/Q3 green: the descriptor for sim.discovery is writable:false configurable:false and a substitution attempt through questEngine.sim or window.__ENGINE draws 0 squares.

secondary_observations.what: FREEZE THE SLOT — one line, and it closes an S38 clause. sim.discovery is assigned plainly at engine.js:435, so the descriptor is writable and configurable. Object.defineProperty(sim, 'discovery', {value: d, writable: false, configurable: false}) closes Q1, Q2 and Q3 together. Named in the round-1 verdict as 'secondary, cheap, and should not wait for a round'; it waited. It matters more under S38 than it did before, because S38 keeps 'the map cannot be made to show you anywhere by anything except a claim to have stood there' as the stronger checkable property — and this route shows squares with no claim to have stood anywhere at all.

THE PIXEL TEST BOTH PRIOR INSTRUMENTS RELY ON MEASURES THE UI CANVAS, NOT THE SCREEN. W1-MAP-r1 C1/C3 and this tool's own first U1/U2 read UISurface.ctx.getImageData and report 'the terrain box holds exactly one colour, channel range [0,0,0]'. True of the UI layer; false of the picture — the panel is drawn at CALM_ALPHA over the running 3D world and the Rootlands are visible through the black box in docs/shots/2026-08-08-critic-map-r2-fresh.png. On the composited frame the same box holds 44 distinct colours. S35's conclusion still holds, but it is carried by screens/map.js:103 skipping undiscovered cells and by drawn_cells = 0, NOT by a colour count. Two controlled arms separate the causes: two EMPTY maps photographed from different standing places differ (44 -> 92 colours, drawn_cells 0 -> 0), and the same place with a walked body differs the other way (44 -> 1855, drawn_cells 0 -> 2911).

THE SAVE CONTAINER'S SEAL IS AN INTEGRITY CHECK, NOT AN AUTHENTICITY CHECK, and nothing says so where it is read. game/src/save/exchange.js computes an unkeyed sha-256 over the canonicalised body: editing sealed bytes is refused, resealing a forged blob with the game's own writer is accepted. Under S38 this is CORRECT and not a defect — S38 rules that the game cannot authenticate the primitive and must not pretend to. It is recorded here only as a one-line comment worth adding, because two rounds of critics have now spent effort discovering it, and because 'the seal does not match' reads to a newcomer like a forgery defence.

TWO DOCUMENTS IN THE TREE STATE OPPOSITE SECURITY PROPERTIES, unchanged since round 1 flagged it, and S38 has now settled which is right. game/src/sim/discovery.js lines 46-50 claim both hard fails 'fail closed against a blob whose every field is under the attacker's control, because the map is a pure function of ONE field'. tools/harness/w1-21-r2-forge.mjs R8 records the opposite and calls it a LIMIT. R8 is right, S38 says so at length, and the header is the one the next author will read.

THE BRIEF'S PREMISE IS OVERSTATED AND THE RECORD SHOULD SAY SO. The dispatch describes W1-MAP-r1 C2/D1/D2/D3 as 'presented as four map failures on a walk whose steps never ran'. They were presented as PASSES: W1-MAP-r1.md §1's table lists all four as passing, and §9 records that they first appeared as failures, that critic-w1-map-stepcheck.mjs reproduced the throw with sim.discovery removed entirely, and that preconditions C0/D0 were added so a walk that did not step could not be filed as a map defect. W1-SAVE-AI.json:91 states it correctly. No false finding was ever published. The re-take was still worth doing and all four survive; the credit belongs to the round-1 preconditions.

I MISSED S38 ON MY FIRST PASS AND IT CHANGED THE SCORE. I grepped ARBITRATION.md for 'S35' and read that row; S38 is the row immediately below it and it amends S35 in place. I found it only when `node tools/ownership.mjs --staged` named an arbiter's staged screenshot. RULES 18 says read the file, and a grep is not reading the file. Nothing measured is affected — the attack was designed and run before the ruling was found — but an entire axis was re-cut afterwards, and a critic who had filed on the first draft would have failed a build for a property a landed ruling says is out of scope.

corpus_extended.what: S38 clause (d) — 'a discrepancy between the blob's claims and the derivation is itemised, not swallowed' — has a gate (S38-4) that can only ever meet the forgery which WRITES claims. The forgery that writes none produces zero in both fields S38-4 reads, on a save that fills the whole province. The clause needs the reachability half stated: an itemisation nothing can read is not an itemisation.
corpus_extended.proposed_clause: Amend S38(d) to: 'a discrepancy between the blob's claims and the derivation is itemised AND the itemisation is published on a surface a probe can read, including the case where the blob makes no claims at all — in which case the derivation's own totals (stood_cells, derived_places, missing_cells) are the itemisation.'

method_deviations.what: The forgery was driven in a live session via importSave() rather than against a cold browser reload.

source_reads.note: Read the wire format (zigzag varint delta trail) in order to deliver a forgery the loader actually parses — a raw bitset decodes to nothing and would have credited the build with a defence it does not have. Afmt proves delivery before any A-result is believed.
Read the draw loop AFTER the pixel measurements, to establish that 'unrendered' is carried by `if (!m.seen(cx,rz)) continue;` rather than by an alpha.
Read after A9 landed, to name what the seal is: an unkeyed sha-256 over the canonicalised body.
